description:
Goal
Finish the work that was intentionally left outside fz-bin after protocol dispatch itself landed.

Signal (unified root)
Investigation collapsed the reduce failures to ONE root: the shared Enum.reduce* bridge callable's surface/return type is not a convergent, identity-correlated fixed point over non-List Enumerables (fz-f98). Its symptoms, all one defect:
- fz-bfh.1 reduce/3 over Range + scalar acc crashes (lane mismatch / driver.rs:971 / transport.rs:2587 missing CallableFlowFact).
- fz-bfh.2 reduce/2 over Range and reduce_while/3 over Map hit settled_callable_boundary "names multiple boundaries".
- fz-bfh.3 reduce/2,3 over Map materialize an absent value (native.rs:2826).
- fz-bfh.4 reduce over Range+Map together never converges (semantic-drive storm).
One non-List shape + a captured callable settles wrong (the crashes); two non-List shapes never settle (the storm). fz-f98 is the single fix; .1-.4 are its regression targets.

Independent items remain:
- fz-x2n delete the dead callable-boundary fallback and fail-loud on multi-surface divergence (a hardening sibling, not the root).
- fz-9i4.7.3 enum_map_family native direct-closure fast-path arity.
- fz-bv3 struct-vs-map nominal dispatch.

Strategy
Fix the root once in fz-f98 (identity-correlated boundary + monotone-convergent surface join), then verify each regression target green on interp + run + build and close it. Do not special-case any Enum helper or Enumerable impl. fz-x2n / fz-9i4.7.3 / fz-bv3 are independent and can proceed in parallel.
title: Retire fz-bin follow-up deferrals
